items.title: Joseph "Fan" Bourgeau Interview, 1972-09-13
items.q: Cooney, I know. A lot of those guys, but I forget their names.

ctx.x: Mm. Did you know a guy named Cooney? Cooney? Yeah. He was a Tom Anderson. There had been a woman. A singer. Cooney? Yeah, I know Cooney. Was it a man or a woman or what? It was a man. Cooney. Did he play an afternoon?

No, I never knew anything to play an afternoon. Cooney, I know. A lot of those guys, but I forget their names. It's like Louis White. When I was in France, I was sitting in the audience and an actress, she must have been a little bit of a woman. She asked, she said, is anybody here from the Orleans? I raised my hand up. I said, yeah, I'm from the Orleans. She said, well, come up here. I'm going to ask you something. And I went up there and I said, what do you want to ask her, miss? She said, I want to ask her,…
Well, this actress knew her, huh?

items.title: Joseph "Fan" Bourgeau Interview, 1972-09-13
items.q: I played with Blue. We had a little band with Blue. Blue was playing with me.

ctx.x: Gayno never had a band. I was the one who knew Gayno how to play in a band. He played after me because I was probably playing this, Johnny Sensei was the first guy who showed me how to play the guitar. And then I switched from guitar to banjo. Johnny Sensei used to play with us too on the Airline Highway. In the 4900, he was on the Airline Highway. We played there. He had a little trumpet called Caledon. He said, I'll be there when you're going to get there. I said, okay. I had playing with him. I had Lawrence's…
What did he play? He played Coney. You mean the guy that was any kind of Blue? No, it wasn't a kind of Blue. No, it wasn't no kind of Blue.
I played with Blue. We had a little band with Blue. Blue was playing with me. He died, boy boy. He drank so much wine, boy boy. He passed away.
